title: ArdaNova production-readiness waves
thesis_health: Materially better than at plan time, and still failing the practical test in named places. What changed: a person signs in, sets up an account and sees 'Ready'/'Not created' with no address and no GUID; /settings/wallets is deleted; the sponsorship flow speaks in stake, sponsors, workers, units and dollars; refusals are consumer English; AZOA's Core/ConsumerSafeErrors actively strips chain vocabulary, base32 addresses and hex digests from rail refusals; the escrow node labels read 'Set Funds Aside' / 'Pay Out' / 'Give Back' / 'Hand On'. What still fails: a member's own credential page says 'Blockchain Status', 'Minted on Algorand' and 'ASA #', and the credential card renders a raw asset id as a mono 'Reference' (OI-54, OI-85); the project Money view renders an engineering refusal naming the node, a tenant credential and two /api/admin routes as the answer to 'where is my money' (OI-51); the funding ask is entered in ARDA with dollars as a caption, which is plan text faithfully implemented and needs an owner ruling (OI-19); AZOA's own sidebar shows every signed-in user a 'DeFi' group with Blockchain/Swap/Bridge (OI-84); and /governance renders the raw enum 'SHARES' and 'total voting power' (OI-49). None of these is a money defect; all of them are the defect the thesis names.

partitions.note: Verified by execution, not by hypothesis: all 11 waves ran as parallel fan-outs against the per-item owns lists in plan.md, each wave's join gate re-grepped the boundaries before launch (AC3), and no wave reported a write outside its declared partition. Where an implementer needed a file it did not own it declared a crossBoundary handoff instead of editing — which is why several items ship as fail-closed seams rather than wired features (see OPEN-ITEMS.md §D). Two partition facts worth carrying forward: test files were in NO item's owns list for the whole program, so new behaviour ships largely unpinned (OI-91); and ardanova-client/prisma/ was owned by too few items, which is how the Wave 6 schema drift (OI-36, OI-37) reached a commit.

owner_questions_note: The review's Q1-Q4 are answered by D44-D47 and Q5-Q7 are carried as stated assumptions. Of the five design questions D44 opened, D49 and D50 answered two (ARDA genesis; the exchange mechanism), recorded in plan.md as design notes N-X1 and N-X2. Four remain open and gate Wave 3: Q-X2 (the ARDA price per US cent), Q-X3 (project-ASA parameters), Q-X4 (who may create a project token), Q-X5 (the off-ramp destination; Stripe Connect platform approval is an unbounded external clock). Q-X6 (who holds a project's ARDA) is ANSWERED in plan.md - a per-project custodial treasury account on the node - because the waves could not be collision-proofed with it open; the owner may reverse it before W3.7 lands.

revisions.what: chain-first re-sequence under D44-D48; the review's fiat-first ordering rejected

critique pass: all 25 RESEQUENCE-CRITIQUE.json findings applied or accepted by name in plan.md's 'Accepted residual risks'; D49/D50/D51 folded in. Two blockers closed - W1.8 teaches the node a production CustodyMode (walletReady was false by construction outside Development, so every downstream wave was silently blocked on the custody the plan claimed to assume), and W3.7 gives each project a custodial treasury account on the node (the exchange credited the platform reserve, leaving the project's funding balance as the Postgres ledger D47 rejected). Wave 8 reordered so the buy-back liquidity policy lands before the user-facing sell path.

CLOSEOUT. All 11 waves executed as parallel fan-outs with per-wave join gates; 53 of 54 items delivered across 18 commits in two repos. Adversarial review per wave: 5 PASS-WITH-DEBT, 6 FAIL. plan.md checkboxes ticked with a per-item status glyph (tick = landed as planned, warning = landed with disclosed stubs or debt, blocked = did not land) and an 'As built' note under every wave. Owner questions Q-X2..Q-X5 closed (Q-X2 settled: ARDA is backing-derived with a 1 ARDA = $0.01 genesis seed, not pegged; Q-X3 resolved by constraint at scale 6; Q-X4 self-serve at publish; Q-X5 Stripe Connect Express). Everything still red, stubbed or found by review is enumerated in OPEN-ITEMS.md as a checkable item with a file:line and an unblock — including 10 open CRITICALs and 16 new instances of the 'a claim in prose is not a control in code' class.

items_not_delivered: W0.4 — publish azoa-sdk (blocked: npm credential 401s; see OPEN-ITEMS.md OI-01)

review_verdicts.note: Every wave shipped and every wave shipped with debt; none closed clean, so no wave heading in plan.md carries a bare tick. A FAIL verdict means the wave's code landed and was committed AND an adversarial reviewer found at least one CRITICAL that is still open — it does not mean the wave was reverted.

open_items.note: Every stub, fail-closed seam, CRITICAL finding, operator action and piece of debt the program left, each with a file:line and its exact unblock. plan.md's per-wave 'As built' notes cite these ids. Read this before starting any follow-up work.
